results.title: Collaborative and privacy-preserving cross-vendor united ...
results.content: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed framework that enables collaborative training of a server model across medical data vendors while preserving data privacy. Driven by these practical issues, we propose a server-rotating FL method (SRFLM) to mitigate the effects of data heterogeneity with multi-vendor datasets and the limitations of a fixed server, thereby achieving the goal of cross-vendor united diagnostic imaging. The classification experiments indicate that our SRFLM has the potential to learn robust representations from heterogeneous data, while the CT image reconstruction results demonstrate its capacity to generate high-quality diagnostic images across different vendors. The experiments demonstrate that by employing the rotational server-communication mechanism and the dynamic server-election strategy, SRFLM more effectively accounts for data characteristics from each vendor and achieves better model convergence in the cross-vendor united CT reconstruction task. This is because the SRFLM can effectively learn vendor-specific data characteristics of each participant through dynamic rotational server adjustments, and improve the overall model performance across different data distributions.
